title: Miło mi pana poznać
focus: formal introductions: pan/pani in every case, państwo, the instrumental

patterns.formal: Formal you: pan / pani / państwo + 3rd person verb
patterns.speaker: Gender follows the speaker

lines.speaker: Ania
lines.pl: Pani|pani_prof profesor|profesor, chciałabym|chcialabym przedstawić pani|pani_dat mojego|mojego kolegę|kolege, Tomasza|tomasza Lewandowskiego|lewandowskiego.
lines.en: Professor, I’d like to introduce my colleague, Tomasz Lewandowski.

lines.speaker: Prof. Malinowska
lines.pl: Bardzo mi miło pana|pana poznać|poznac. Ania dużo mi o panu|panu opowiadała|opowiadala.
lines.en: Very nice to meet you. Ania has told me a lot about you.

lines.speaker: Tomek
lines.pl: Mam nadzieję|nadzieje, że same|same dobre rzeczy. Czym|czym się pani zajmuje|zajmuje, jeśli mogę zapytać?
lines.en: Only good things, I hope. What do you work on, if I may ask?

lines.speaker: Prof. Malinowska
lines.pl: Jestem językoznawczynią|jezykoznawczynia. Zajmuję|zajmuje1 się fonetyką|fonetyka języków|jezykow słowiańskich|slowianskich.
lines.en: I’m a linguist. I work on the phonetics of Slavic languages.

lines.speaker: Tomek
lines.pl: Co za zbieg okoliczności|okolicznosci! Mój brat robi doktorat z fonetyki|fonetyki w Poznaniu|poznaniu. Może go|go pani zna|zna?
lines.en: What a coincidence! My brother’s doing a PhD in phonetics in Poznań. Perhaps you know him?

lines.speaker: Prof. Malinowska
lines.pl: Lewandowski… Oczywiście, Marek! Byłam|bylam w jego|jego komisji|komisji w zeszłym|zeszlym roku|roku. Proszę|prosze go ode|ode mnie pozdrowić|pozdrowic.
lines.en: Lewandowski… Of course, Marek! I was on his committee last year. Please give him my regards.

lines.speaker: Prof. Malinowska
lines.pl: Może usiądą|usiada państwo|panstwo z nami? Zaraz podają|podaja kolację|kolacje.
lines.en: Would you like to sit with us? They’re about to serve dinner.

lines.speaker: Tomek
lines.en: With pleasure. Thank you for the invitation.

pani_prof.gloss: Mrs., madam; formal “you” to a woman
pani_prof.tags: noun · feminine · vocative singular (same form as nominative)
pani_prof.why: In direct address Polish uses pan or pani with a title and no surname: pani profesor, panie doktorze, pani dyrektor. “Profesor Malinowska” on its own would not be used to address her.
pani_prof.compare: To a male professor: Panie profesorze.

profesor.tags: noun · masculine form referring to a woman · not declined
profesor.why: When profesor refers to a woman, it doesn’t decline: pani profesor (vocative), z panią profesor (instrumental). Referring to a man, it declines fully: panie profesorze, z panem profesorem.
profesor.compare: The feminine profesorka exists, but in academic address pani profesor is the norm.
profesor.history: From Latin professor, “one who declares publicly.”

chcialabym.tags: verb · imperfective · conditional · 1st person singular · feminine
chcialabym.why: The conditional makes an offer or request polite: chciałabym przedstawić, “I’d like to introduce.” Plain chcę would sound abrupt in this setting.

you.f: You would say: chciałabym przedstawić…, as Ania does.

pani_dat.why: Przedstawić kogoś komuś: the person being introduced is in the accusative, and the person they’re introduced to is in the dative. Pani looks the same in the dative.

mojego.why: For masculine nouns denoting people or animals, the accusative singular has the genitive form: mojego kolegę. With an inanimate noun it matches the nominative: mój dom.

kolege.tags: noun · masculine, declined like a feminine -a noun · accusative singular
kolege.why: Kolega ends in -a, so it takes the -ę of feminine -a nouns in the accusative. The adjective with it is still masculine: mojego kolegę.
kolege.compare: Other masculine -a nouns: mężczyzna, poeta, kierowca.

tomasza.tags: proper noun · masculine personal · accusative singular
tomasza.why: Masculine personal nouns take the genitive ending -a in the accusative. Ania uses the full name, Tomasz, because the setting is formal; among friends he’s Tomek.

parts: -ego (the i marks k softened before e)
lewandowskiego.why: Surnames in -ski, -cki and -dzki decline like adjectives: Lewandowski, Lewandowskiego, Lewandowskiemu. A woman of the same family is Lewandowska.

pana.why: Poznać takes a direct object in the accusative, and for pan the accusative has the genitive form: pana.
pana.compare: To a woman: Miło mi panią poznać.

you.m: People meeting you will say: Miło mi pana poznać.
you.f: People meeting you will say: Miło mi panią poznać.

poznac.gloss: to meet; to get to know
poznac.why: Poznać is a perfective of znać: “to come to know,” and so “to meet for the first time.” Afterwards you know each other: znamy się.

panu.why: O meaning “about” takes the locative: o panu, o pani, o nim. Panu is also the dative, as in dziękuję panu.

opowiadala.tags: verb · imperfective · past · 3rd person singular · feminine
opowiadala.why: Feminine because the subject is Ania. Imperfective because the telling happened repeatedly or over time; third person has no person marker.

nadzieje.why: Polish says “to have hope”: mieć nadzieję. Nadzieja is the direct object of mieć, so it’s accusative.

same.why: Before a plural noun, sam means “nothing but”: same dobre rzeczy, “only good things.” Rzeczy is feminine, so the ending is non-virile -e.

parts: stem of co in the oblique cases
czym.why: Zajmować się takes the instrumental (zajmuję się fonetyką), so the question word is instrumental too. Czym się pani zajmuje? is the polite way to ask about someone’s work.
czym.compare: Other forms of co: czego, czemu, o czym.

zajmuje.why: Third person because it agrees with pani. Verbs in -ować form their present tense with -uj-: zajmować → zajmuje, dziękować → dziękuje.

jezykoznawczynia.why: After być, a noun saying what someone is goes in the instrumental: jestem językoznawczynią, jestem nauczycielem.
jezykoznawczynia.compare: Some women prefer the masculine form: jestem językoznawcą.

you.f: You would say: Jestem językoznawczynią (or językoznawcą).

zajmuje1.why: The answer to Tomek’s question, in the first person. Present-tense forms don’t mark gender, so this is the same for everyone.

fonetyka.why: Instrumental because zajmować się requires it.
fonetyka.history: From Greek phōnētikós, from phōnḗ, “voice, sound.”

jezykow.why: Fonetyka języków: the genitive does the work of English “of.”

slowianskich.why: Adjectives agree with their noun: języków is genitive plural, so słowiańskich. After k and g the ending is spelled -ich in place of -ych.

okolicznosci.why: Zbieg okoliczności, literally “a running-together of circumstances,” is the everyday word for “coincidence.” The second noun is genitive.
okolicznosci.history: Zbieg comes from zbiegać się, “to run together, converge.”

fonetyki.why: Z plus the genitive names the subject of a degree or exam: doktorat z fonetyki, egzamin z matematyki. Contrast z przyjemnością at the end, where z means “with” and takes the instrumental.

parts: stem Poznań- (ń spelled ni before a vowel)
poznaniu.why: W plus the locative. Masculine nouns ending in a soft consonant take -u in the locative: w Poznaniu, w pokoju.
poznaniu.history: Usually derived from an old personal name, Poznan, related to poznać, “to get to know.”

go.why: Go is the unstressed accusative of on. Short pronouns like go, mu and mi tend to come early in the clause, here right after może.
go.compare: Stressed form, or after a preposition: jego, dla niego.

zna.why: Third person to agree with pani. Znać is for knowing people and things; wiedzieć is for knowing facts.

bylam.why: The professor is speaking about herself, so the feminine ending -a.

jego.why: Jego, “his,” is the genitive of on and never agrees with its noun: jego komisja, w jego komisji, jego brat.
jego.compare: Her: jej. Their: ich. Both are invariable too.

komisji.why: W plus the locative. Nouns in -ja take -i in the locative, genitive and dative: komisja → komisji. Here komisja is the doctoral examining committee.

zeszlym.why: W zeszłym roku, “last year,” is locative after w.
zeszlym.history: Zeszły comes from the past form of zejść, “to go down, pass”: a year that has gone by.

roku.why: Stems ending in k, g or ch take -u in the locative: w roku, w bloku, w parku.

prosze.why: Proszę plus an infinitive is the polite way to ask someone to do something: proszę usiąść, proszę go pozdrowić. It avoids the imperative, which can sound brusque in formal speech.

ode.why: Before mnie, od becomes ode to break up the consonant cluster. Other prepositions do the same: ze mną, we mnie, beze mnie.

pozdrowic.why: Pozdrowić kogoś od kogoś means “to give someone regards from someone.” The root is zdrowy, “healthy”: greeting someone was wishing them health.

usiada.why: Third person plural to agree with państwo. Może usiądą państwo…? works as a polite invitation: “perhaps you’ll sit…?”

panstwo.why: Państwo is the formal “you” for a group, especially a mixed one. It takes a third-person plural verb: usiądą państwo, czy państwo się znają?
panstwo.compare: Państwo meaning “state, country” is spelled the same but is a neuter singular noun.
panstwo.history: Both meanings go back to pan, originally “lord, master.”

podaja.tags: verb · imperfective · present · 3rd person plural · no stated subject
podaja.why: With no subject, a third-person plural verb means people in general, like English “they’re serving dinner.”

kolacje.why: The direct object of podają, so accusative.
kolacje.history: From Latin collatio, “a bringing together”; in Polish it’s the evening meal.

parts: suffix -ość (ć spelled ci before a vowel)
przyjemnoscia.why: Z meaning “with” takes the instrumental: z przyjemnością, “with pleasure.” In doktorat z fonetyki, z takes the genitive and means something different.

dziekujemy.why: Tomek thanks her for both himself and Ania, so he uses “we.”

zaproszenie.why: Dziękować za plus the accusative: to thank for something. Zaproszenie is the verbal noun of zaprosić, “to invite.”

exercises.prompt: Say what you do: “I’m a teacher” (nauczyciel / nauczycielka). Jestem ___.

explain.m: After być, the instrumental: nauczyciel + em.
explain.f: The feminine nauczycielka in the instrumental: nauczyciel + k + ą.

exercises.hint: Look at jestem językoznawczynią. Which case follows jestem? Then check the learner setting at the top.

exercises.prompt: Introduce Marek’s sister, Ewa Lewandowska: Chciałbym przedstawić Ewę ___.
exercises.explain: Women’s surnames in -ska decline like feminine adjectives, so the accusative is -ą.
exercises.hint: Lewandowski becomes Lewandowskiego, like an adjective. What does a feminine adjective do in the accusative?

exercises.prompt: Say to a woman you’ve just met: Miło mi ___ poznać.
exercises.explain: The accusative of pani is panią: pan + ią, where the i marks the soft ń.
exercises.hint: To a man it’s pana. What happens to pani after poznać?

exercises.explain: Zajmować się takes the instrumental: składnia → składnią.

exercises.prompt: Ask a couple politely whether they know each other (znać): Czy państwo się ___?
exercises.explain: Państwo takes a third-person plural verb: znają.
exercises.hint: Look at może usiądą państwo. Which person does the verb take?
